page_title: Resiliency Planning for High-Traffic Events - Shopify

summary.name: Resiliency Planning for High-Traffic Events
summary.one_liner: A Shopify engineering blog post describing how the team prepares its platform for high-traffic events like Black Friday Cyber Monday through load testing, resiliency matrices, game days, and incident analysis.
use_cases: Preparing a platform for peak traffic events
Running regular load tests to catch regressions
Learning from incidents without blaming a single root cause
Slowing change before a major sales weekend
summary.what_it_does: The article explains Shopify's approach to resiliency ahead of Black Friday Cyber Monday. It describes regular load and stress testing to find regressions and new system limits, including comparing differently configured shops. It covers a user-centric resiliency matrix that maps dependencies and failure modes to expected user experience, and game days that test whether the documented model matches production behavior. It also covers incident analysis that avoids single root-cause attribution, and reducing the rate of change before peak weekend.
notable: Describes a user-centric resiliency matrix for documenting expected user experience under dependency failures
Uses game days to compare the documented system model against real behavior
Slows change and shifts engineering time toward performance and reliability before BFCM
Accompanies a Shipit! talk video on building a culture of resiliency
caveats: Describes Shopify's internal practices, not a downloadable tool or product
Article does not give detailed tooling names or step-by-step instructions
